name: Uzzah
overview: Uzzah was a male figure in the biblical narrative known primarily as the son of Abinadab. He is notably remembered for his death resulting from touching the ark of the covenant, an event that underscores the holiness and reverence required in handling sacred objects. His story is concise but significant within the context of the Old Testament.
namesAndTitles: The name Uzzah, also rendered as Uzza, means 'strong, fierce one' in Hebrew. This name reflects a sense of strength or might, although it was not given by God. Both variations appear in Scripture with the same meaning, highlighting the consistency of his identity across biblical texts.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Uzzah was the son of Abinadab. Beyond this father-son relationship, no additional family connections or tribe affiliations are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Uzzah's significance lies in his tragic death as a direct consequence of touching the ark of God, which was forbidden and demonstrated the seriousness of God's holiness. His story serves as a solemn reminder of the need for obedience and reverence toward God's commands, particularly concerning the sacredness of the ark. This event marks a pivotal moment in the transportation of the ark and highlights divine holiness in the biblical narrative.
